feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications/strategy roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads professionally and is rich in relevant detail, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital strategy leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure and advancement at NACo signal trust, growth, and domain expertise.  
- Good use of specifics: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, studio buildout, and the 10,000+ page migration add substance and technical depth.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve focus and save space.  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; include results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix writing/style consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“workflows, and systems” vs. “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting. No major misspellings found, but there are minor stylistic inconsistencies and some dense phrasing.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around leadership, modernization, and mission-driven impact would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad channel list with a tighter mix of leadership, modernization, and operational strengths.
- Add one clearer differentiator, such as advocacy/public-sector communications or translating policy/technical issues.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy and stakeholder communications, with a proven ability to turn technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies.
- The channel list duplicates detail reinforced throughout Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy/governance, content/workflows, analytics/optimization, stakeholder/advocacy, multimedia/events.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout; avoid mixing broad functions with tactical tasks.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & public-sector communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “workflow,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “advocacy communication” repeat language already covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” may feel redundant given the detailed Technical + IT section.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new in the consultant scope, especially AI search, platform improvement, and enterprise workflow design.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and cross-channel content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-focused phrasing: “Designed/implemented” instead of “build and refine” or “deliver.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and foreground distinctive work: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search success/engagement gains, or teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current bullets repeat prior NACo themes: governance, workflows, Drupal, analytics, and cross-channel communications.
- Avoid re-stating website management/history already covered under Director of Digital Media; emphasize consulting, modernization, and AI/search work instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-value leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational impact, and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one sharper achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel and analytics bullets outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, efficiency, reporting cadence, or decision-making impact if available.
- Tighten studio/governance language: “Launched NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” and “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep the higher-level strategic oversight here, leave recurring newsletter management to the earlier role.
- “Governance/workflows” also appears in the current consultant role; frame this entry as enterprise leadership and implementation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, ownership, and concrete channel impact without repeating website/governance points covered more strongly in the Director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper leadership line: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for county officials nationwide.”
- Combine newsletter detail with outcome: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving consistency and cadence of member communications.”
- Make the video bullet more active: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow bullets with one stronger line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing processes that improved coordination among communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/standards bullet.
- “Expanded video” may duplicate the earlier Digital Media Manager role unless framed here as formalizing it into a recurring channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

Suggested edit:

- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership

- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and vaguer than the governance/operations strengths evidenced in recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reorder for impact: lead with recent differentiators, then core platforms.  
- Replace generic list with: “Drupal • CMS modernization & migration • AI-enabled search experiences • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable systems • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Tighten phrasing: change “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)” or remove entirely if kept in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “CMS modernization for 10,000+ page environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line for line; keep Topline Skills higher-level, not tool-exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

- GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role.

- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/relevance and trim lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: put Drupal first and consider grouping by proficiency or use case.
- Replace the flat list with a tighter version such as: “Drupal (enterprise CMS migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add one concrete qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views environment)”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was only lightly used; it weakens the enterprise/public-sector CMS focus.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- If both sections remain, use this item for platforms only and keep modernization/AI/search/API language in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/platform modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, tag management, edge/serverless scripting, CI/CD
- Replace older/versioned terms with cleaner phrasing: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in brief: “used for front-end implementation, analytics tagging, lightweight automation, and deployment workflows”
- Consider dropping “jQuery” to the end or removing it if no longer central to current work; prioritize modern/recent tools

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep it here only if framed as CI/CD rather than general automation

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation is already emphasized elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the actual mix of platforms.
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier are the real automation stack, lead with those and demote or trim generic collaboration tools.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to impact in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., automated editorial intake, approvals, reporting, or cross-team coordination).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello overlap as project tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise communications operations, this item should signal scale, lifecycle/CRM relevance, and strongest/current tools first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by likely relevance/enterprise weight: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, make the label more strategic: “Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms”
- Add brief functional qualifiers instead of just names, e.g. “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)”
- If one platform was primary in recent NACo work, put it first and consider dropping the least relevant tool to keep the section tighter.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid repeating operational detail here.
- “Engagement” may partially duplicate “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless this item stays clearly focused on email/CRM platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-stage team building, production, and workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Split into concrete contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- Tighten production language: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded the organization’s in-house multimedia output.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or size of team supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this item, frame it as launching or early production support rather than expansion.
- “website refresh” may feel redundant with the later 10,000+ page redesign; keep this as a smaller refresh or platform improvement, not a major transformation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications; partnered across teams to turn research into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast launch the headline achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or types of multimedia assets created.
- Consider a concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications, translating findings into digital and multimedia content. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, guest coordination and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing that overlaps with later digital media roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia generally; later entries already cover that progression.
